dsl_findings.claim: the wfdsl and councilspec expression grammars are NOT co-extensive, so a council-stage stopping rule can only satisfy both by using councilspec registry metric names with registry-legal enum tokens
dsl_findings.evidence: custom:ideas_added_after_barrier -> councilspec.parse OK, wfdsl.expr.parse raises "unexpected character ':' at offset 6" = a DSL-SEM-007 VIOLATION. risk_verdict == BLOCK -> wfdsl OK, councilspec raises "enum metric needs one of the schema enum tokens". The councilspec registry has 52 metric names and 15 global enum tokens.
dsl_findings.consequence: councilspec's own documented extension mechanism (custom:<name>) is unusable from inside a DSL council stage. All council stopping rules here are written in the intersection, which is why advisories are 0 of 12.

dsl_findings.claim: the wfdsl expression grammar has NO arithmetic operators, so a reconciliation like a == b + c cannot be expressed
dsl_findings.evidence: "verdicts_returned + null_lenses == personas_requested" -> DSL-SEM-007 violation "unexpected character '+' at offset 18"
dsl_findings.consequence: such conditions must be pre-computed by the runner and asserted as a single identifier (bp-cnc-01 uses unaccounted_personas == 0). Not a defect, but it is undocumented and cost a validation round here.

dsl_findings.claim: the DSL confidence_band enum is narrower than the design corpus's CONF vocabulary, so a card graded very-likely is DOWN-graded when expressed in the DSL
dsl_findings.evidence: workflow-dsl.schema.json#/$defs/confidence_band = [almost-certain, likely, roughly-even, unlikely, remote] (5 members); 09-WORKFLOW-BLUEPRINT-LIBRARY.md declares 6 (adds very-likely and very-unlikely). estimate.confidence="very-likely" is rejected with an enum error.
dsl_findings.consequence: 4 of these 12 carry a corpus band of very-likely; each records the corpus band verbatim in x_extensions.confidence_band_note and carries the nearest legal band in the field, so no confidence claim is silently widened.
